recommendation.unit: Bound a source-owned decomposition of the actual legacy admission source guard, starting with a real historical repair guard node and its actual upstream legacy source parent, with CJS guard adaptation only when the complete actual graph is proved.
recommendation.why: The observed guard is executed in three phases and contains an actual wide repair guard plus other independently scoped checks. A leaf alone will not remove its repeated invocation while executeSource still runs the full opaque CJS guard in physical preflight/final, so do not claim a leaf-only performance benefit. This unit targets a sampled actual owner route, not an inferred constructor-only bottleneck.
recommendation.implementation_gate: Keep current complete genuine CJS guard as whole fallback until the same constructed subjects expose authentic nodes for all original guard subcalls and the CJS tools/assertBound wrapper is equivalently represented. Do not install empty physical nodes for opaque original/currentSass/tool dependencies or flatten by matching file paths. Preserve distinct independently constructed instances and consumed callbacks, with global preflight then consumption then final across exact identity dependencies.
recommendation.local_repair_contract: Cold/final read fresh via repair physical policy for every actual bound ref and check captured SHA and length; consume checks each provided callback byte sequence against fresh physical bytes under existing semantics and applicable before/after physical checks. Share same-instance reentry lock and restore on exceptions. Keep side operations/projections independent; no current byte, parsed-source, verdict or receipt cache, no public reader grant. This is a design target, not a complete drop-in proof.
recommendation.parent_contract: Preserve exact original/currentSass physical policies, dynamic boundary reads, product population and no-link behavior, CJS tools/bound duplicate guard scopes, actual supplied callback semantics and all local and nested finals after every callback. If child nodes cannot be authentically captured or policies cannot be represented, retain whole original guard.

counterexamples: A same-path reference may have a logical historical projection but physical current bytes; equality of path cannot authorize merging these operations.
A supplied callback mutates an earlier member or adds/removes a product file while a later member is read: final full union and population must reject it.
Peer package symlink or wrong package identity can pass a generic file hash sweep while failing the currentSass peer policy.
An alternate scheduler plan entered during a dependency callback must reject on the active actual dependency and recover after an exception.
Independent factories may hold equal references with distinct callbacks or capture times and cannot be deduplicated.
verification_needed: Differential actual guard callback observations and fault injection for cold, every consumed byte, late mutation, final union, product population, peer policy, physical versus historical projection, exceptions/reentry, and opaque/mismatched fallback.
Confirm exact source/guard identities and finite helper authentication; original CJS constructor and all source inputs stay genuinely qualified.
After implementation and focused tests, measure the same workload independently; no speedup or full owner outcome follows from sampled stacks.
limitations: Static design only. No maintained edits, tests, producers, owner runs, or new performance measurements. Other hot stacks (roster, frame sweeps, constructors) remain visible; priority can change after direct validation.
